title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§40 of 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets', ms. p. 314). Grothendieck has been working in the discrete/transcendental setting. The thrice-punctured line U_{0,3}^an is uniformized as D/π(2), with D the upper half-plane and π(2) the level-2 congruence subgroup (Γ(2) mod ±1). On the previous page he 'normalizes' a homomorphism (73) into an effective one by choosing the lifts of the elliptic points P = -j and P̄ = -j̄ so that τ over P is a root of unity. He then regrets lacking the foundations to redo these constructions for profinite groups, in particular a profinite theory of 'tronçons' ('jonglage de tours' for profinite groups with loop structure).

This page begins by calling something 'triviale' (the sentence starts on the previous page). He then says it is nonetheless in this direction that one should find a group-theoretic ('gruppentheoretisch') understanding of the homomorphism (40): M̂_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 ≃ [target of the isomorphism uncertain]. He calls this homomorphism the main motivation of the present § and the previous ones.

Modern reading. The most natural interpretation is the map from an arithmetic or profinite 'modular' group attached to (0,3) to GL_2(Ẑ)/±1. Such a map is cut out by the Tate module of the Legendre / universal elliptic curve. The geometric part goes to (P)SL_2(Ẑ) through the congruence completion, and the determinant is the cyclotomic character. The quotient by ±1 accounts for the automorphism -1 of elliptic curves. 'Gruppentheoretisch' understanding would then mean recovering this representation purely from the profinite free group π̂_{0,3} (rank 2, three loop classes with product 1) together with its outer automorphism data, without using the elliptic curve. This reading is plausible but not certain, since the meaning of M̂_{0,3} is not fixed on this page.

He says this should prompt renewed thought on the passage to the profinite context. He then pinpoints a logical priority. The question whether the constructions of the § extend to the profinite context *without* adding 'arithmetic' structure is subordinate to another question. That added structure would be a subgroup Π ⊂ Autext_lac(π̂_{0,3}), i.e. outer automorphisms preserving the loop (inertia) classes, satisfying more or less sensible conditions such as congruence relations (from §38).

The next page states the subordinate question. Are these congruence relations genuinely arithmetic, specific to outer actions coming from Π_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q)? Or are they more or less automatic consequences of an 'algebraic provenance' formalism for profinite groups, valid as in the discrete case? He proposes to extract such a formalism experimentally. §41 then studies whether an isomorphism Π̂^1_{0,3} ≅ Ĝ^+_{0,3} commutes with the Π_Q-action, and computes outer automorphisms of Π̂_{0,3} and Ĝ^+_{0,3}.

In modern terms the page sits squarely in the problem of characterizing the image of Gal(Q̄/Q) in Out(F̂_2) by group-theoretic conditions on inertia-preserving outer automorphisms. Drinfeld and Ihara later answered this in part with the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂, whose defining relations play the role of the conditions envisaged here. The specific question raised — whether such relations are arithmetic or formal consequences of profinite 'algebraic provenance' — is a form of the 'Gal = GT̂?' problem.
errors: No mathematical error can be asserted. The displayed isomorphism 'GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 ≃ PGL(1,Ẑ)' as transcribed cannot be right, since PGL(1) is trivial. The target is a misreading; the manuscript seems to show something like 'GP(1,Ẑ)' or 'GSp(1,Ẑ)'-type notation. GL(2)/±1 is not PGL(2) either, so the intended right-hand side is unclear.
The sentence is incomplete: the page ends mid-argument ('est subordonnée : elles'). The subordinate question is only stated on the next page.

ideas.what: Seek a purely group-theoretic description of the homomorphism from the (0,3) modular/fundamental group to GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 (Tate-module type representation), i.e. derive it from the profinite free group with its loop structure.
ideas.modern_name: Profinite / congruence description of the Galois representation attached to the Legendre family; action of GT̂ / Gal on profinite completions of SL_2(Z) and its congruence quotient
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and Gal action on π̂_1 of P^1-{0,1,∞}; this specific homomorphism is not explicitly there as far as I know

ideas.what: Arithmetic structure given by a subgroup Π ⊂ Autext_lac(π̂_{0,3}) of loop-preserving outer automorphisms satisfying relations (congruence-type) as substitute for the Galois group
ideas.modern_name: Inertia-preserving outer automorphisms; Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂ as a group-theoretic approximation to Gal(Q̄/Q)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), in outline; La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: Methodological question: are the congruence relations satisfied by Galois outer actions specifically arithmetic, or formal consequences of an 'algebraic provenance' formalism for profinite groups?
ideas.modern_name: Whether Gal(Q̄/Q) → GT̂ is surjective; anabelian characterization of 'geometric origin' of outer actions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara's question / Drinfeld; Grothendieck's anabelian program
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in Esquisse and the 1983 letter to Faltings; the precise dichotomy is not stated there as far as I know

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly wants a profinite theory of 'tronçons' (tower juggling for profinite groups with loop structure) to transfer the discrete uniformization constructions (Γ(2), elliptic points, normalized homomorphism) to the profinite setting. He states that this is subordinate to deciding whether congruence relations on Galois outer actions are arithmetic or formal. The profinite 'tronçon' formalism itself does not seem to have been developed as such.
missed.quote: la question s'il y a une (extension des constructions du présent §, au contexte profini) indépendamment de l'introduction d'éléments de structure "arithmétiques" ... est subordonnée
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a formulation of the problem of finding group-theoretic conditions on Out(F̂_2) that are formally forced, versus those specific to Gal(Q̄/Q). It is close in spirit to the Gal vs GT̂ question, but phrased via a congruence-subgroup / uniformization route. That route (lifting Γ(2)-uniformization data profinitely) is less explored than the braid/pentagon route.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows, apparently around 1981 and before Drinfeld–Ihara, Grothendieck framing the image of Gal(Q̄/Q) in inertia-preserving outer automorphisms via relations, and asking whether those relations are arithmetic or formal. This anticipation of GT̂ is broadly known from the Esquisse. The specific route via the GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 homomorphism and profinite 'tronçons' is a modest unpublished detail, but no finished result appears on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'qui est la motivation principale du réflexions du présent §, et des précédent' → 'qui est la motivation principale des réflexions du présent §, et des précédents'
'relations [?] exponentielles' should read 'relations congruentielles' (consistent with the next page: 'Si ces relations congruentielles...').
'PGL(1,Ẑ)' is doubtful; the image shows something like 'GP(1,Ẑ)' or possibly 'GSp(1,Ẑ)'. The hat/caret on M̂_{0,3} sits over the '3'/top right ('M^{^}_{0,3}').

The inserted line 'la question s'il y a une' replaces a crossed-out symbol after 'que'. The reading is 'je me rends compte dès maintenant que la question s'il y a une (extension des constructions du présent §, au contexte profini), indépendamment ...'.
'(40)' appears to be the equation/paragraph label next to a heavily crossed-out symbol with subscript '0,3'.
